docs.flippable.component: `Flippable` is the turn — as DATA, and the engine's flip effect does the turning. A flip is not
«swap one surface»: it is GEOMETRY (a reflection the children inherit) plus, sometimes, CONTENT
(the other face is a whole other subtree). One toy field could model a card and none of the rest,
so the atom holds the four data a turn needs and leaves the DOING to a recipe.
```ts
import { node, Bounded, Surfaced, Flippable, installStockFlips } from "game-kit"
installStockFlips()   // the recipes, and the effect that turns a node over
const card = node("aceCard",
Bounded({ bounds: rect(1, 1.4) }),
Surfaced({ surface: "queen" }),
Flippable({ flip: "turnOver", back: "tartan", turns: 1 }))
## The four fields
- `flip` — the recipe NAME in `render/flips.ts`. `mirror` reflects and swaps nothing; `turnOver`
reflects AND shows the back surface. Empty is `mirror`.
- `turns` — how many turns from the authored state. It SUMS along the chain, and the current side
is the parity: even is face-up, odd is over. Never a stored boolean.
- `axis` — the reflection line in degrees, a PARAMETER — 90 a Y-mirror, 76 a 76° one. Not a preset
per angle: that is the `Axis76` lesson, a magnitude is a field, not a new record.
- `back` — the down-side surface a swap recipe reveals. Empty falls back to the front, so a token
identical both sides needs no back and a half-built card never turns up blank.
## Two parities, and case A
The reflection follows a node's OWN turns; the content swap follows the SUMMED turns up the chain.
That split is what makes a re-flipped card in a flipped stack come out right by itself. Flip a stack
and every card shows its back (summed odd) and mirrors with the stack (inherited reflection). Turn
one card back and its summed parity is even again — face-up — while its own reflection and the
stack's cancel, so it is upright too. No per-card bookkeeping anywhere; the arithmetic resolves it.
## Why a recipe and not the pixels
What a turn DOES lives in a registry, the mirror of `surfaces`. `mirror` is pure geometry; `turnOver`
swaps the surface. A card, a knight, a stack, a whole desk each pick their own recipe, and a new one
is a registration rather than a branch anything has to learn. The engine mixes the chosen recipe in
through the effects list and knows none of them by name.
## Reflection is not a pose
A reflection has determinant −1, and no scale-rotate-move composes one. So it is not folded into a
pose (the canon says a spec holds no reflection); it is composed separately, by parity, at apply
time — exactly the way a summed `z` is read and never stored. Two of them cancel exactly, which is
the whole of case A.
docs.flippable.card: One card. Drag `turns`: even is face-up, odd shows the back AND mirrors — the two together are a
real turn, the determinant passing through zero as the card goes edge-on.
`flip` picks the recipe. `turnOver` swaps to the back surface and reflects; `mirror` only reflects,
so a symmetric card looks unchanged — the mirror is doing its work, there is just nothing asymmetric

docs.flippable.arena: A container turned over. The reflection is inherited through the chain, so the arena's children
mirror WITH it — the row of tiles comes back in reverse screen order. Nothing walks the tree; the
geometry composes down it, the same way a child's position does.
Change `axis` and the mirror line turns with the whole arena. This is the half a single card cannot
show: a flip is not a property of a face, it is a reflection of a frame, and everything in the frame
docs.flippable.stack: Case A, the one that broke every toy model. A stack turns its cards: `turns` SUMS along the chain,
so flipping the stack shows every card's back and mirrors each with the stack.
Turn on `reflipOne` and the second card turns once MORE. Its summed parity is even again, so it is
face-up while its neighbour stays over — and its own reflection and the stack's cancel, so it is
upright, not doubly mirrored. Nobody wrote «this card is special»; the parity of `turns` resolved
it. That is the whole reason the side is a summed count and not a stored flag.
docs.flippable.knight: A piece with a face. The muzzle sits to one side, so the mirror is visible on a single node: turn
it and the knight looks the other way. Nothing is swapped — `mirror` is pure geometry, and the
asymmetry is what reveals it. A symmetric token under the same recipe would look unchanged, with
`axis` tilts the line the piece turns about: 90 is a Y-mirror, 76 turns it about a slanted line —
a parameter of the instance, never a recipe per angle.

docs.flippable.decks: Two decks, one turn. The left flips as ONE PHYSICAL THING — `deckReorder`: the order reverses
with the cards. The right is the keep-order alternative — `deckChildren`: cards turn in place.
Each card keeps its own back tint, so the difference stays readable face-down.
Neither recipe touches a card: the backs come from the SUMMED parity, each card answering with its
OWN recipe. The deck's recipe owns exactly one thing — whether the order is part of the turn.
docs.flippable.nested: A tray holding a lone card, a reordering deck and a keep-order deck. One turn of the TRAY sums
into everything, and each node answers with its OWN recipe: the card turns over, one deck
reverses, the other does not. No branch anywhere asked what kind of node it was.
`reflipOne` turns the lone card once more: its summed parity is even again — face-up amid a turned
world, its two reflections cancelled. Case A, live, in mixed company.

Drag the drift with the board turned and the mirrored pawn answers in real time. This is the case
a readable `directionFlip` row gives up — see the Row scene for the trade.
docs.flippable.row: The same row twice, one turn. Above, `mirror`: the tiles come back reversed AND each is reflected
— the corner dots jump sides, the way glyphs would. Below, `directionFlip`: the order reverses and
nothing mirrors, so the dots stay put and a word would stay readable.
The trade is real. The mirror keeps hand-moved offsets turning (case D); the direction flip loses
them and keeps the content legible. The NODE picks, by naming its recipe — a mechanism is data,
never a branch in the engine.
docs.flippable.emptyback: A `turnOver` card whose `back` is empty. The turn falls through to the front — mirrored, because
the geometry still happens — and never a blank: `flip.back || front` is the rule, so a half-built
card stays visible while its art is on the way.
A token identical on both sides simply needs no back at all — the empty string is that statement,
